# Private full-key attention CPU fixtures
<!-- cspell:words steminfer testdata webgpu SDPA unfused softmax einsum WGSL readback GOMAXPROCS VECLIB OPENBLAS BLAS Solovyev -->

This development slice records synthetic post-RoPE, single-head attention inputs and actual native/original CPU outputs. It enables no application route or model selection. The initial CPU checkpoint enabled no Worker or GPU dispatch; the later source-only bridge below remains unexecuted on hardware. Its source branch remains based on frozen `d705f6d`; newer main documentation is not replaced or relabeled by this private checkpoint.

The 28 preregistered cases use queries `[m,64]` with `1 <= m <= 8` and keys/values `[N,64]` with `1 <= N <= 1723`. Every query attends to all keys. Ragged boundaries, full-key tails, ties, cancellation, high dynamic range, directed-rounding boundaries, subnormal inputs and FTZ resurrection are separate cases. The ceiling is 32 cases and 64 MiB of new producer/reference/log output.

## Actual references and separate probes

`attention_fixture_test.go` calls the unchanged native `multiply`, `attentionSoftmax` and `multiply` functions. The observed backend was Apple Accelerate. Source arrays, raw QK, final probabilities and PV output are saved. It loads no model, weights or audio. Native fused softmax internals are not exposed or imitated.

`attention_oracle.py` executes the exact MIT original `Attend` module at commit `6fdad13686bb7e84d029ec66f9dbe76e65c93ebf`, SHA-256 `c7abbc40a3fd20ff7f6001fa9f8ee9ad5df6452272712a5e719b8f8468bf2223` (4,410 bytes). See the package LICENSE/NOTICE. The recorder separately calls its evaluation-mode math endpoint and CPU SDPA endpoint with no dropout. Read-only observers capture the actual math endpoint's einsum and dropout input. Eight additional explicit PyTorch operations are labeled unfused probes: raw QK, multiplication by 1/8, maximum, subtraction, exponential, positive denominator, division and PV. They are not claimed to expose SDPA or fused softmax internals. No checkpoint deserialization is needed.

The original source remains a checksum-pinned, developer-supplied input, recovered from [the pinned upstream file](https://github.com/ZFTurbo/Music-Source-Separation-Training/blob/6fdad13686bb7e84d029ec66f9dbe76e65c93ebf/models/bs_roformer/attend.py). The current code retains Roman Solovyev's MIT attribution.

## Numeric design and limits

The [dated WGSL specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-WGSL-20261021/#floating-point-accuracy) permits directed rounding, reassociation and arithmetic input/output FTZ. The new contract uses the full adjacent Float32 interval, not a nearest-only half-ULP assumption. Its dot diagnostic includes its own conservative Float64 accumulation error and a directed-rounding `2^-23` budget. Compensated Float64 is not an exact-real oracle. A positive-series exponential enclosure uses outward Float64 steps, 18 terms and at most 15 squaring steps, rather than treating `Math.exp` as exact. GPU exponential/division design envelopes use the specification's argument-dependent ULP budgets.

`classifyStages` recomputes raw dots and each unfused stage from exact submitted operands/previous stored stages. File-provided error budgets or sum-of-absolute-products do not exist. Stage corruption is rejected. Saved native/original endpoints remain separate diagnostics, never bound authority. Whole-file SHA-256 checks bind their provenance. Source underflow is retained even when an observed value is zero. A dyadic-grid test also limits potentially subnormal dot partial sums. The initial CPU checkpoint left propagated uncertainty for later work. The source-only extension below derives complete source-to-output intervals; independent mathematical/hardware review remains open.

The mandatory case has four query lanes of 16, tail key lanes of -10.9375 and tail values of 32. Raw QK is -700; the scaled tail is -87.5. Actual CPU probes record exp/probability `9.982351397596697e-39` and final `3.194352447230943e-37`. Actual native Go, original math and CPU SDPA produce that final value too. The fixture is always underflow-limited: a legal GPU flush could remove a subnormal probability that later produces normal output. Fabricated unit traces with zeroed exponential/probability/output remain limited.

## Prospective resource plan

The 16 MiB application-buffer cap is a declared future ownership envelope, not measured GPU/driver residency. Let `C=m*N`, `O=64*m`, `I=O+128*N`, `S=5*C+2*m+O`, and `F=24+4*(I+9*C+4*O+2*m)`. Charged bytes are `5*F + 4*(4*I) + 10*(4*S) + 65,536 + 524,288`: file snapshots/checksum/transfer, input staging, stage/readback/interval copies and fixed capture overhead. The maximum is 13,848,280 bytes. A later Worker must prove this lifecycle, canaries, disposal, no queue, cancellation and device limits before hardware execution.

CPU reference work uses coarse product-term and stage-element visits: `2*m*N*64 + 12*C + 2048*m`, maximum 1,946,144 under 2,097,152. Compensated reduction and fixed series operations cost more machine instructions; payload validation visits are separately disclosed by `payloadScanFloatCount`. This is not a CPU timing guarantee.

The closed GPU budget counts floating data arithmetic and reduction comparisons, including padded invocations, with multiply-add terms charged twice. It excludes integer indexing/control, loads/stores, barriers and scheduling; the extension below records a separate source-level integer bound. Let `P64=64*ceil(N/64)` and `P256=256*ceil(N/256)`:

| Planned observable pass | Charged work |
| --- | --- |
| Raw QK | `2*m*P64*64` |
| Scale | `m*P64` |
| Maximum | `m*(P256+255)` |
| Shift | `m*P64` |
| Exponential | `m*P64` |
| Denominator | `m*(P256+255)` |
| Probability | `m*P64` |
| PV | `2*m*64*N` |

The total maximum is 3,621,872 under 8,388,608. Actual-M dispatch is required; the old 64-row GEMM pair would charge 14,155,776 slots even before the other stages. The initial checkpoint had no attention shader. The later shader is source-only: no actual compiler, dispatch or timing has demonstrated this plan.

## Recorded CPU checkpoint

The actual exporters and independent CPU auditor exited zero in 5.684 seconds total. Go/original/auditor outer times were 3.871/1.551/0.260 seconds, with sampled aggregate child RSS 142,737,408/210,763,776/73,891,840 bytes. Limits were 30 seconds per process, two minutes total, 1 GiB sampled child RSS and 64 MiB new output; no limit was exceeded. Original PyTorch 2.8.0 used one intra/inter-op thread. Native policy was configured with `GOMAXPROCS=1`, `VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1`, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1` and `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`; opaque BLAS worker count was not observed. Its upstream deprecated SDPA-context warning is retained.

All 28 actual endpoint/probe fixtures passed the CPU stage audit: 25 ordinary-input diagnostics and three underflow-limited cases. Maximum actual Go-versus-original-math and CPU-SDPA-versus-math differences were each `1.71661376953125e-5`; unfused-probe-versus-math maximum was `1.52587890625e-5`. These are distinct observations, not a universal endpoint parity tolerance. Eight Node contract tests and the Go registry check passed. Raw sources, traces, source checksums, monitor logs and per-case plans remain in ignored `artifacts/private-stems/recovery-20261023/attention-cpu-20261023-v1/`.

GPU ownership/dispatch and full propagated-stage proof remain open. No model forward, audio processing, GPU operation, public activation or complete attention qualification is claimed. Earlier 70-case GEMM, 32-case normalization, watchdog/software-adapter failures and musical/model-conditioning limitations remain unchanged historical evidence.

## Source-only eight-stage bridge checkpoint

The next private slice adds `attention.wgsl` and its exact pinned literal `shader.mjs`, a closed fixture index, a disposable Worker, a parent owner and a combined local/propagated checker. It imports no production component and fetches no model, shader or fixture. No attention GPU API, WGSL compiler, audio or neural model was executed for this checkpoint. Dummy interfaces in source tests are explicitly synthetic.

The eight separate compute passes store every stage. Raw QK dispatches `ceil(N/64)` groups across actual query rows; PV dispatches one group across each actual row and loops over all keys. Max and denominator use 256-lane reductions with a 1,024-byte workgroup array. Every input and stage has two guards; all eight stages and six input guards are copied back. Shape products, maximum indices, storage/binding/workgroup limits, exact canary geometry and finite written cells are checked. A source checksum pins the literal shader; the model contract identifies the unchanged F16 archive and original Attend commit, without loading either model or weights.

At the maximum shape, expected created GPU buffers total 1,440,000 bytes. The conservative full application-buffer envelope remains 13,848,280 bytes. Its five fixture copies include caller Blob, raw read, private snapshot, transfer and digest input. Input staging receives four input-size allowances. Ten stage-size allowances cover GPU/readback/returned buffers, Float64 endpoint pairs, Int16 grid metadata, initialization and diagnostic storage, plus fixed guards/capture slack. The module-global reduction array is conservatively charged even for entries where a compiler might eliminate it. All 216 groups in the largest dispatch receive 1,024 bytes, totaling 221,184 prospective workgroup bytes inside the existing 524,288-byte slack; 303,104 bytes remain for bounded capture/metadata. No simultaneous hardware residency or compiler elimination is assumed. This is logical application-owned buffer admission, not measured process RSS or opaque driver residency.

The FP data/reduction-comparison budget remains 3,621,872 under 8,388,608. An additional conservative integer indexing/control bound is 30,842,624 at the closed maximum shape: raw `16*m*P64*64+32*m*P64`; PV `16*m*64*N+32*m*64`; scale/exp each `16*m*P64`; shift/division each `32*m*P64`; max/sum each `m*(16*(P256+255)+64*256)`. These source bounds exclude loads/stores/barriers and are not compiler instruction counts or GPU performance claims. Calling the FP cap a total GPU arithmetic cap would be incorrect.

The parent reserves the full envelope before Blob reads, snapshots, hashing or transfer. Only exact registered file sizes/hashes, ABI, request ID and model/source identities can advance. One active fixture or retained receipt is allowed, with no queue. Cancellation rejects promptly, but read/hash work that cannot be canceled keeps its lease until actual settlement. Transient reads are detached. A readable result retains its lease; `dispose()` detaches stage/bound/grid aliases before releasing. Abort after resolution does the same. A five-second deadline requests cancellation, then terminates the Worker after 50 milliseconds. Destruction/termination is cleanup, not proof of prompt GPU preemption. Worker success is posted after its buffers/device are destroyed; adapter absence is RED, and fallback/software status is disclosed.

`propagated.mjs` combines both raw and PV dot diagnostics with uncertain-input corner sums in the same admitted term traversals. It never calls historical `classifyStages` as an extra full reference pass. Compensated Float64 diagnostics retain outward rounding errors. Dyadic-grid metadata proves exact zero or normal-spaced intermediate sums stay outside the subnormal range under sum reassociation and FMA: rounding an exact dyadic multiple either preserves it exactly or rounds to a coarser grid. Scaling by 1/8 adjusts that grid; selection/subtraction retain the common grid. Continuous intervals crossing zero therefore do not automatically imply subnormal realizability. Source/subnormal inputs and actual or possible finer grids remain LIMITED.

Propagation follows raw QK, scale, maximum, shift, exponential, positive F32 reduction, division and PV. Exp/division budgets use the maximum ULP across the entire argument/result interval, so a power-of-two boundary cannot shrink the bound. Exp uses the specification's `3+2*abs(x)` ULP allowance plus one outward enclosure ULP. An argument below -4096 receives an explicit outward subnormal envelope, never a silently clamped lower value; outside the proved [-8192, minimum-normal] domain it is rejected. A matching maximum leaves at least one exponential near one even with allowed FTZ, giving a normal positive denominator. Underflow flags follow original sources and propagated intermediate intervals even when observed results are zero. The mandatory resurrection fixture remains LIMITED.

The 33 source units passed, including ordinary all-zero/tie/dyadic controls, full-key tail influence, stage corruption, interval boundaries, closed ABI/guards, memory admission/settlement/disposal, late Worker messages and dummy device loss/cancellation. A controlled all-zero classification RED and a dummy lost-device RED remain preserved. The latter exposed a resolved-promise race; persistent device-loss state now overrides another already-resolved operation. This is unit evidence, not a real device result.

The final indexed source-checkpoint checker audited all 28 unchanged saved CPU probe files in 0.458623375 seconds with sampled child RSS 82,870,272 bytes; the monitor observed exit zero and no limit violation. The earlier 0.839-second / 83,918,848-byte audit remains preserved under `draft-audit/`; it is not the final indexed measurement. It again classified 25 ordinary-input diagnostics and three LIMITED cases. Maximum term visits were 1,764,352; declared coarse reference work remains at most 1,946,144. Payload/reference validation scans are reported separately. Interval-corner/compensated arithmetic and up to three fixed 18-term exponential enclosures per score cost additional instructions within the same charged traversals. The widest propagated output interval was 1.1562547870063664; that is uncertainty, not an endpoint parity tolerance. Native Float64-denominator, original math, CPU SDPA and unfused endpoints remain separate observations.

New proof files are isolated under ignored `artifacts/private-stems/recovery-20261023/attention-source-20261024-v1/`; the accepted CPU v2 index and all older raw proofs remain unchanged. Independent source/ownership/numeric review and a separately authorized hardware fixture run are still required. Full-model/browser inference, performance, broader musical quality and public activation remain open.

## Receipt ownership correction — source only

Independent QA reproduced two disposal escapes in the initial source checkpoint: deleting/replacing bounds or grid map entries hid their original buffers, and an own `byteLength: 0` property hid a live ArrayBuffer. Both original peer probes and RED logs remain preserved in the separate ignored `attention-receipt-fix-20261024-v1/` proof directory. The original source checkpoint index and older raw artifacts are unchanged.

The parent now remembers each original backing buffer privately at acquisition and freezes that closed inventory before publishing a receipt. Disposal uses module-captured intrinsic byte length and transfer operations, skips truly detached buffers, detaches every remaining original and verifies their lengths before releasing the lease. It never discovers ownership from caller-visible maps or typed-array `buffer` properties. Frozen bounds/grid/reason containers provide additional defense. Three new regressions cover map deletion/replacement, view and ArrayBuffer property shadows, partial prior detachment, repeated disposal and abort after receipt delivery. All three failed against the old source; the full corrected source suite passed 36/36 in 145.508541 milliseconds. These are CPU units with fake interfaces, not hardware evidence.

The fix changes receipt metadata/lifetime only; shaders, input pins, numeric interval calculations and budgets are unchanged. No saved CPU exporter, GPU, audio, model, inference or benchmark was rerun. Source/ownership review remains required before any separately authorized hardware fixture run.

## Source-only capture harness

The private page accepts exactly one registered local numerical fixture File at a time. It serves no fixture over HTTP and uploads no bytes. Fourteen checksum-bound assets have literal GET/HEAD routes; startup refuses a changed asset set, size or digest. Other paths, nonzero request bodies, unsupported methods, foreign Host/Origin and cross-site requests are denied. CSP permits only same-origin scripts/styles/workers/images, with `connect-src 'none'`. No server, browser, adapter or GPU was started for these checks.

The page keeps its disposable receipt in a module-private closure. Its raw-stage preparation hash runs before summary or chunk allocations: the maximum is 277,792 raw bytes plus 16,384 control bytes and 4,096 hash allowance, totaling 298,272. The subsequent capture phase uses 2,048-byte chunks with exactly one in flight. Its conservative logical representation budget is two numeric-array copies at 32 bytes per entry (131,072), two UTF16 decimal protocol copies including fixed headers (36,864), three byte/write/hash copies (6,144), fixed control/summary storage (65,536) and hash allowance (4,096): 243,712 bytes. The phases are exclusive and each fits the existing 303,104-byte capture slack; the maximum leaves 4,832 bytes. This is application-owned representation admission, not a VM heap or process RSS guarantee.

Only a bounded summary is serialized: at most 8,192 characters of JSON, closed fields, bounded strings/features/reasons and fixed limit names. Full bounds/grids and receipt buffers are never exposed through the page bridge. The complete raw-stage SHA-256 appears in the header; every chunk carries capture ID, sequence, offset, total and its own hash. The parent rejects gaps, overlap, stale or duplicate messages and corrupted bytes. It snapshots each small write, hashes incrementally, closes the writer and independently streams the closed file through another hash before success. Numeric evidence uses random private directories (0700) and literal files (0600), never a source filename. Output admission remains at most 64 MiB, with a 6 GiB free-disk reserve.

The parent acknowledges completion only after all writes, hashes and file closure settle. The page then disposes the receipt and waits its exact-run settlement latch before clearing session authority. Early caller rejection is not settlement; delayed read/hash and later-run controls cover that distinction. Cancellation during parent work retains the receipt until actual parent cleanup acknowledges closure. An unconfirmed cleanup cannot invent a release. The injected driver launches no process or browser. Batch admission is at most four distinct registered cases in 60 seconds; an external reviewed process guard remains required.

The exact five shared [qualification ownership helpers](../../../../../../scripts/qualification/README.md) were reused from commit `188385980aea78aa180c883f6055d151b6af6add`, with per-file hashes in `scripts/qualification/provenance.json`. They were not modified or executed in this source wave. The Chair's prior sixteen synthetic helper controls are separate attributed evidence. Actual normal/crash browser ownership controls remain a separate gate; no second OS process framework or launcher was introduced.

Executed source checks: 49 Node units passed in 489.646875 milliseconds with test concurrency one; three pure Python source/handler tests passed without binding a socket. New source evidence is isolated under ignored `artifacts/private-stems/recovery-20261023/attention-harness-source-20261024-v1/`. All earlier indices and raw proofs remain unchanged. Rerun only these source controls with pinned Node 26.12 and Python: `node --test --test-concurrency=1 internal/audio/steminfer/testdata/webgpu/attention/*.test.mjs` and `python3 internal/audio/steminfer/testdata/webgpu/attention/test_capture_server.py`.

The ordinary-sandbox visible Brave launcher, actual process ownership observations, shader compilation, adapter/hardware identity and 28 existing hardware fixture captures are still unexecuted in this checkpoint. They require separate review and release. No model, audio, benchmark or public feature is activated.


## Capture acquisition ownership repair

Independent peer QA found a missing boundary in the original capture source checkpoint: the driver awaited the file-sink factory before opening parent ownership. If acquisition created a partial resource and setup cleanup failed before a handle returned, the driver treated the absent sink as closed and disposed the receipt. The exact peer probe/log and a controlled regression against the unchanged old driver are retained in `attention-acquisition-fix-20261024-v1/`. The old checkpoint/index and every earlier raw proof remain unchanged.

The driver now opens the page's parent lease before invoking any sink factory. The factory must synchronously return a complete managed handle; the driver captures its bound `acquire`, `write`, `finish` and `abort` methods before the first acquisition await. File construction performs no I/O. All acquisition runs in its exact retained task, so its failure cannot hide the cleanup handle. A missing, throwing, asynchronous or incomplete factory never grants an absent-handle closure inference. A successful abort must explicitly report `closed: true` after acquisition, writes, verification and all cleanup actually settle. Cleanup failure retains the page lease and receipt.

The file sink privately owns both the writer and independent verification reader, retaining each handle until its close succeeds. Failed close, file removal or directory removal leaves cleanup retryable and admission held. Successful abort is idempotent; it refunds its reservation once. Admission uses a private owner token so aborting an older completed sink cannot clear a newer sink's ownership. The injected file-operation table exists for source-controlled tests only. The small fixed handle/method/state records use the existing logical control allowance; they add no raw copies and do not change capture, memory, disk or work caps.

All 58 source units passed in 415.363417 milliseconds with concurrency one. Regressions include factory rejection, explicit unconfirmed abort, cancellation during acquisition, delayed acquisition/close, partial files, separate close/file/directory failures, verification-reader close failure, method replacement, repeated abort and older/newer ownership. The first reader injection incorrectly matched read-only flags without no-follow and missed its intended failure; that test-setup RED is preserved, and the corrected selector exercises the close failure. Assertions and cleanup requirements were not weakened. These are injected/source controls and tiny private numerical files, not hardware evidence.

No server, socket, browser, GPU API/compiler, process helper, model, audio, inference or benchmark ran. The fourteen served asset hashes, exact 28 fixture pins, shaders, numeric intervals and five reused helper files are unchanged. Independent source review remains required; the actual launcher/ownership/hardware gate is still held. Rerun the source suite using pinned Node 26.12: `node --test --test-concurrency=1 internal/audio/steminfer/testdata/webgpu/attention/*.test.mjs`.


Private attention launcher preparation now reuses the accepted Node admission helper and observed-survivor helper verbatim from `51d206c`. The shared OwnedGroups core remains SHA-256 `d5a9978835c7ebcd6fd9c30c6074f4e55b84ac26683b66c4f9198daf3dd08a40`; no group-membership or signaling framework was forked. Prior helper versions remain bound to their immutable indices, and current per-file hashes/origins are recorded in `scripts/qualification/provenance.json`. Three mocked Node admission controls passed in this source wave; they launch no browser and do not rerun or replace the earlier sixteen process controls. Actual launcher/hardware qualification remains held.
